cp.hero.title: Retrieve a credential.
cp.hero.lede: A trusted Java application asks a Credential Provider on the host for a Vault credential at request time. The Provider authenticates the calling application by its **hash** (plus OS user and path) — no stored password, no client certificate.
cp.scenario.authorized.label: Expected success
cp.scenario.authorized.desc: A caller whose application hash IS registered on the App, reading a Safe it may access → the credential is returned.
cp.scenario.authorized.ev1.lead: Authenticated by application hash, not a key.
cp.scenario.authorized.ev1.body: The Credential Provider measured the calling jar's hash (plus OS user and path) and matched it to a registered Application — no client certificate, no stored password.
cp.scenario.authorized.ev2.lead: The full secret never left the host.
cp.scenario.authorized.ev2.body: The caller hashed the credential on the host; only a 6-char preview, its length, and SHA-256 crossed the bridge into the cluster.
cp.scenario.authorized.ev3.body: The App is provisioned for PIN-SEC-DEMO only; every other Safe is denied at the authorization layer.
cp.scenario.invalid-hash.label: Expected authentication failure
cp.scenario.invalid-hash.desc: A DIFFERENT jar whose hash is NOT registered on the Application → the Credential Provider rejects it at the application-authentication layer.
cp.scenario.invalid-hash.ev1.lead: The hash did not match a registered Application.
cp.scenario.invalid-hash.ev1.body: The rogue jar has a different application hash (and install path). The provider logs APPAP133E — the calling application is unauthorized.
cp.scenario.invalid-hash.ev2.lead: Rejected before any Safe was touched.
cp.scenario.invalid-hash.ev2.body: Authentication failed first, so no Safe authorization was evaluated and no credential was returned.
cp.scenario.invalid-hash.ev3.body: Only the exact registered jar can retrieve. Recompiling or moving it changes the hash and is rejected — as designed.
cp.scenario.denied.label: Expected authorization failure
cp.scenario.denied.desc: A registered caller, but a Safe this Application is NOT permitted to read → the Credential Provider denies it at the authorization layer.
cp.scenario.denied.ev1.body: The caller's hash/OS-user/path matched a registered Application, but that App is not a member of the requested Safe.
cp.scenario.denied.ev2.lead: Least privilege at the Safe boundary.
cp.scenario.denied.ev2.body: Being a valid application is not enough — the App must also be granted the specific Safe. It was not, so the request was refused.
cp.scenario.denied.ev3.body: The denial happened in the vault; nothing was returned to the caller or the cluster.
cp.scenario.dual.label: Dual account · expected success
cp.scenario.dual.desc: A registered caller queries a dual-account pair → the Credential Provider returns whichever account is ACTIVE. On rotation the other goes active — zero downtime, no app change.
cp.scenario.dual.ev1.body: The query fronts a dual-account pair by virtual username; the provider returns whichever account is currently active.
cp.scenario.dual.ev2.body: When the active account rotates to its partner, the same query resolves to the new active account — no code or config change.
cp.scenario.dual.ev3.body: As with every CP retrieval, only the preview + length + SHA-256 of the active account's secret cross the bridge.

ccp.hero.title: Retrieve via REST.
ccp.hero.lede: The app authenticates to the Central Credential Provider with a **client certificate** (mTLS) and fetches a credential over REST — no Vault password or API key stored on the workload.
ccp.scenario.authorized.label: Expected success
ccp.scenario.authorized.desc: Valid client certificate, and a Safe this Application IS permitted to read → the credential is returned over REST.
ccp.scenario.authorized.ev1.lead: Authenticated by certificate, not a key.
ccp.scenario.authorized.ev1.body: The app proved its identity with a client certificate mapped to a registered Application — no static API key or Vault password on the workload.
ccp.scenario.authorized.ev2.body: Only a short preview + hash is shown; the full credential is never logged or written to disk.
ccp.scenario.authorized.ev3.body: The App is provisioned for PIN-SEC-DEMO only; every other Safe is denied at the authorization layer.
ccp.scenario.no-cert.label: No certificate · expected authn failure
ccp.scenario.no-cert.desc: The app connects WITHOUT a client certificate → AIMWebService rejects it at the authentication layer (this denial is the point).
ccp.scenario.no-cert.ev1.body: AIMWebService requires mutual TLS. Without a client certificate there is no Application to authenticate — APPAP227E.
ccp.scenario.no-cert.ev2.lead: Rejected before any Safe was touched.
ccp.scenario.no-cert.ev2.body: Authentication failed at the door; no Safe authorization was evaluated and no credential was returned.
ccp.scenario.no-cert.ev3.body: Require SSL + client certificates on the AIMWebService site is exactly what turns an anonymous call away.
ccp.scenario.denied.label: Denied safe · expected authz failure
ccp.scenario.denied.desc: Valid client certificate, but a Safe this Application is NOT permitted to read → AIMWebService denies it at the authorization layer.
ccp.scenario.denied.ev1.body: The certificate mapped to a registered Application, but that App is not a member of the requested Safe.
ccp.scenario.denied.ev2.lead: Least privilege at the Safe boundary.
ccp.scenario.denied.ev2.body: A valid certificate is not enough — the Application must also be granted the specific Safe. It was not, so the request was refused (APPAP004E).
ccp.scenario.denied.ev3.body: The denial happened server-side; nothing crossed back to the workload.
ccp.scenario.dual.label: Dual account · expected success
ccp.scenario.dual.desc: Query a dual-account pair by custom property → AIMWebService returns whichever account is ACTIVE. On rotation the other goes active — zero downtime, no app change.
ccp.scenario.dual.ev1.body: The query fronts a dual-account pair by virtual username; AIMWebService returns whichever account is currently active.
ccp.scenario.dual.ev2.body: When the active account rotates to its partner, the same query resolves to the new active account — no code or config change.
ccp.scenario.dual.ev3.body: As with every CCP retrieval, only the preview + hash of the active account's secret is shown.
swa.hero.title: Reach the database by identity.
swa.hero.lede: This workload stores **no credential**. It proves who it is with a short-lived SPIFFE SVID; the gateway authorizes by **SPIFFE ID** before Postgres is ever reached.
swa.scenario.trusted.label: Trusted workload
swa.scenario.trusted.desc: Issued a valid SVID, passes mTLS, and its SPIFFE ID is allow-listed at the gateway → it reads the shipments database.
swa.scenario.trusted.ev1.body: The workload proved who it is with a short-lived SPIFFE SVID issued by the trust domain — no static API key or password anywhere.
swa.scenario.trusted.ev2.lead: Authorized by SPIFFE ID at the gateway.
swa.scenario.trusted.ev2.body: ghostunnel allow-lists the exact SPIFFE ID before the connection reaches Postgres; identity is the authorization.
swa.scenario.trusted.ev3.body: The SVID is ephemeral and rotates; there is no credential on disk to steal or rotate manually.
swa.scenario.untrusted.label: Untrusted workload
swa.scenario.untrusted.desc: Holds a valid SVID, but its SPIFFE ID is NOT allow-listed at the gateway → rejected during the mTLS handshake, before Postgres.
swa.scenario.untrusted.ev1.body: The workload has a genuine SVID from the same trust domain — but the gateway's allow-list does not include its SPIFFE ID.
swa.scenario.untrusted.ev2.body: Same CA, valid certificate — the gateway rejects the handshake purely because the SPIFFE ID is not permitted.
swa.scenario.untrusted.ev3.body: The connection was refused at the gateway; Postgres was never reached.
swa.scenario.unknown.label: Unknown workload
swa.scenario.unknown.desc: The node attests, but no registration policy matches this workload → the SWA server refuses to issue an SVID. With no identity, it cannot even attempt the resource.
swa.scenario.unknown.ev1.body: The SWA server has no node-group selector matching this workload, so it declines to mint an SVID at all.
swa.scenario.unknown.ev2.body: Without an SVID there is nothing to present at the gateway — the request never leaves the starting line.
swa.scenario.unknown.ev3.body: Only workloads whose ns/sa match a registration entry receive an identity — everything else is unknown by design.
swa.scenario.foreign.label: Foreign trust domain
swa.scenario.foreign.desc: A workload from a foreign trust domain (acme.courier) presents a self-signed identity → rejected at the mTLS trust boundary; no federation is configured.
swa.scenario.foreign.ev1.lead: Signed by a CA you don't anchor.
swa.scenario.foreign.ev1.body: The peer presented a valid certificate — just from a foreign trust domain. Without federation, your trust roots don't anchor it.
swa.scenario.foreign.ev2.body: The mTLS handshake failed at the door; no SVID exchange, no gateway authorization, no database access.
swa.scenario.foreign.ev3.body: acme.courier still has its own identity — your trust roots simply do not anchor it. SWA trust-domain federation would resolve this.
conjur.jwt.brand.name: Open Standard · JWT
conjur.iam.brand.name: Native Platform · AWS STS
conjur.hero.title: Fetch a scoped secret.
conjur.hero.lede.jwt: The workload presents a **JWT-SVID** to Secrets Manager (authn-jwt). Secrets Manager validates it against the trust-domain JWKS, returns a **short-lived, scoped** access token, and the app reads a variable — no stored API key.
conjur.hero.lede.iam: The workload signs an **sts:GetCallerIdentity** with its instance-profile role (via IMDS). Secrets Manager replays it to AWS (authn-iam), verifies the ARN, and returns a **short-lived, scoped** access token — no static AWS secret, no API key.
conjur.scenario.authorized.label: Authorized retrieval
conjur.scenario.authorized.desc.jwt: Present a JWT-SVID → Secrets Manager authenticates it (authn-jwt), grants a scoped token, and the app reads the in-scope variable.
conjur.scenario.authorized.desc.iam: Sign an STS caller identity → Secrets Manager verifies the ARN (authn-iam), grants a scoped token, and the app reads the in-scope variable.
conjur.scenario.authorized.ev1.body.jwt: The app authenticated with a JWT-SVID from SWA — no static API key and no long-lived credential.
conjur.scenario.authorized.ev1.body.iam: The app authenticated with a signed sts:GetCallerIdentity from its instance-profile role — no static AWS secret, no Secrets Manager API key.
conjur.scenario.authorized.ev2.body: Secrets Manager returned an access token scoped to a limited set of variables; it expires quickly and is held only in memory.
conjur.scenario.authorized.ev3.body: Only a short preview + hash is shown; the full secret is never logged or written to disk.
conjur.scenario.invalid.label: Invalid credential · expected authn deny
conjur.scenario.invalid.desc.jwt: Present an invalid or expired JWT (bad signature / wrong audience / expired) → Secrets Manager's authn-jwt validation rejects it before any token is issued.
conjur.scenario.invalid.desc.iam: Present a tampered or expired STS request (or an ARN mapped to no host) → Secrets Manager replays it to AWS, AWS rejects it, and authn-iam fails before any token is issued.
conjur.scenario.invalid.ev1.body.jwt: Secrets Manager checked the JWT against the trust-domain JWKS and required claims (issuer, audience, expiry) — it did not pass.
conjur.scenario.invalid.ev1.body.iam: Secrets Manager replayed the sts:GetCallerIdentity to AWS; AWS rejected it (bad or expired signature), or the verified ARN maps to no Secrets Manager host.
conjur.scenario.invalid.ev2.body: Authentication failed before any access token was issued — nothing was authorized and nothing was read.
conjur.scenario.invalid.ev3.body.jwt: A forged or expired JWT can't be minted without the trust domain's signing key — the boundary holds.
conjur.scenario.invalid.ev3.body.iam: Secrets Manager doesn't take the caller's word for it; it re-verifies the identity with AWS on every request.
conjur.scenario.denied.label: Out of scope · expected authz deny
conjur.scenario.denied.desc: Authentication succeeds and a scoped token is granted — but the token is NOT authorized to read a variable outside its scope → Secrets Manager refuses the read (403).
conjur.scenario.denied.ev1.body: The access token may only read the variables its Secrets Manager policy grants — this one is outside that set.
conjur.scenario.denied.ev2.body: Even a valid identity and token cannot read arbitrary secrets; the token is scoped to specific variables by policy.
conjur.scenario.denied.ev3.body: The read was refused (403 Forbidden); nothing crossed back to the workload.

viz.topo.boundary.untrusted.title: Authorization boundary
viz.topo.boundary.untrusted.body: The workload holds a valid SVID, but its SPIFFE ID is not allow-listed at the gateway. ghostunnel refused the mTLS connection before Postgres was ever reached.
viz.topo.boundary.unknown.title: Identity boundary
viz.topo.boundary.unknown.body: No registration policy matched this workload, so the trust domain declined to mint an SVID. With no identity, it could not even attempt the gateway — as designed.
viz.topo.boundary.foreign.title: Trust boundary
viz.topo.boundary.foreign.body: The peer presented an SVID from a different trust domain. Its trust root does not anchor to this domain, so the connection was rejected at the boundary.
viz.topo.boundary.trusted.title: Retrieval failed
viz.topo.boundary.trusted.body: The workload's identity checks out, but the database read through the SPIFFE gateway did not complete — check the SWA agent, the ghostunnel gateway, and Postgres reachability.
viz.topo.boundary.denied.title: Authorization boundary
viz.topo.boundary.denied.body: The caller was authenticated, but the Application is not a member of the requested Safe. Nothing was returned.
viz.topo.boundary.no-cert.title: Authentication boundary
viz.topo.boundary.no-cert.body: No client certificate was presented. AIMWebService requires mutual TLS — rejected at the door, as designed.
viz.topo.boundary.invalid.title: Authentication boundary
viz.topo.boundary.invalid.body: The workload's signed identity was not accepted by the authenticator. Authentication failed before any variable was read — no scoped token was issued.
viz.topo.boundary.default.title: Authentication boundary
viz.topo.boundary.default.body: The calling application's hash is not registered on the Application. Rejected before any Safe was evaluated — as designed.
viz.layers.boundary.untrusted: The workload holds a valid SVID, but its SPIFFE ID is not allow-listed at the gateway. The mTLS connection was refused before Postgres was reached.
viz.layers.boundary.unknown: No registration policy matched this workload, so the trust domain refused to issue an SVID. With no identity, it never reached the gateway.
viz.layers.boundary.foreign: The peer's SVID comes from a different trust domain; its trust root does not anchor here. Rejected at the trust boundary.
viz.layers.boundary.trusted: The workload's identity checks out, but the database read through the SPIFFE gateway did not complete. Check the SWA agent, gateway, and Postgres.
viz.layers.boundary.denied: The caller was authenticated, but the Application is not a member of the requested Safe. No credential was returned.
viz.layers.boundary.no-cert: No client certificate was presented; AIMWebService requires mutual TLS. Rejected before any Safe was evaluated.
viz.layers.boundary.invalid: The workload's signed identity was not accepted by the authenticator. Authentication failed before any variable was read — no scoped token was issued.
viz.layers.boundary.default: The calling application's hash is not registered. Rejected before any Safe was evaluated — as designed.
